# Status Indicator Dots Accessibility Design Plan > **For Claude:** Use a11y-planner protocol. Review with a11y-critic after implementation. > **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA > **Users who need accessibility:** Screen reader users, keyboard-only users, low vision users, high-contrast mode users > **Assistive technologies:** NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, keyboard navigation **Feature:** Reusable `` component indicating status via color in sidebars, tables, and card headers. **Risk Level:** Low (static indicator) / Medium (color-only failure risk if unaddressed) **Component/Page Type:** Presentational/Status Icon Component --- ## Phase 1 — Scope & Context - **What is being built?** A reusable status indicator dot component used across an internal ops dashboard. - **User need:** Quick visual status check for tasks, team members, and deployments without reading surrounding text. - **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA - **Assistive tech requirements:** NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver must announce the semantic status (not the visual shape/color). Keyboard users must not be trapped or confused by non-interactive elements. - **Risk factors:** Color is currently the sole indicator → fails WCAG 1.4.1. Compact mode hides text labels → risks complete loss of meaning for non-sighted users if not handled programmatically. - **Constraints:** Design system colors/shapes must remain unchanged. Component must support both full-label and compact modes without conditional DOM restructuring. ## Phase 2 — Semantic Structure Plan The dot conveys semantic status information; it is **not decorative**. It must be marked up as an image/icon per WCAG 1.1.1. **Structure Stub (React/JSX):** ```jsx {/* Primary pattern: role="img" on the dot element itself */} ``` **Why this structure?** - `role="img"` explicitly tells ATs this element conveys information, not decoration. - Avoids `
` or `` without roles, which screen readers ignore for meaning. - Satisfies WCAG 1.1.1 (Non-text Content) and 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value). ## Phase 3 — Interaction Pattern Design - **Interactive?** No. This is a static status indicator. - **APG Pattern:** None required. Static indicators do not follow interactive APG patterns. - **Keyboard model:** Not applicable. The dot must never receive focus. If used inside an interactive row/card, the parent element handles keyboard activation. ## Phase 4 — Focus Management Plan - **Focusable?** No. `tabIndex` is omitted (defaults to `-1` for non-interactive elements). - **Focus traps/management:** None. The component does not open overlays, modals, or dynamic panels. - **Note:** If the dot is placed inside a focusable parent (e.g., a table row or card), ensure the parent's focus indicator remains visible and is not obscured by the dot's background color. ## Phase 5 — State Communication Design | State | Visual Indicator | Programmatic Indicator | ARIA Attribute | WCAG Citation | |-------|-----------------|----------------------|----------------|---------------| | Active (green) | Green fill | `aria-label="Active"` | `role="img" aria-label="Active"` | 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value | | Warning (yellow) | Yellow fill | `aria-label="Warning"` | `role="img" aria-label="Warning"` | 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value | | Error (red) | Red fill | `aria-label="Error"` | `role="img" aria-label="Error"` | 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value | - **Live regions?** Not required. Status is static and announced once on mount/focus via `aria-label`. - **State changes:** If status updates dynamically (e.g., deployment completes), update `aria-label` synchronously. No `aria-live` needed unless the change occurs outside user expectation (rare for status dots). ## Phase 6 — Visual Accessibility Plan 1. **WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color (Core Failure):** - Current design fails because color is the sole indicator. Users with color vision deficiency or high-contrast mode cannot distinguish status. - **Requirement:** `aria-label` carries the semantic meaning regardless of visual color changes. 2. **WCAG 1.4.11 Non-Text Contrast:** - The dot must have ≥3:1 contrast ratio against its adjacent background color (not just white). - **Action:** Audit design system hex values against all valid dashboard backgrounds (light, dark, table row hover, card header). If any combination falls below 3:1, adjust `colorHex` or add a subtle border/shadow. 3. **High Contrast Mode (Windows):** - Windows HCM may replace custom colors with system black/white. The dot may lose its color entirely. - **Mitigation:** `aria-label` ensures meaning is preserved. Test with Windows HCM enabled to verify screen reader still announces status correctly. ## Phase 7 — Content Accessibility Plan 1. **Accessible Name Strategy (Chosen Pattern):** - **Selected:** `role="img"` + `aria-label` on the dot element itself. - **Justification:** Works identically in full-label and compact modes without conditional DOM. Avoids double-announcement risks. Satisfies WCAG 1.1.1 & 4.1.2 cleanly. `title` is explicitly rejected (WCAG 4.1.2: unreliable across ATs, not announced by default). 2. **Compact Mode Handling:** - When text labels are hidden for visual noise reduction, the dot must still convey meaning. - **CSS technique:** Use standard visually-hidden class (`clip: rect(0 0 0 0); clip-path: inset(50%); height: 1px; margin: -1px; overflow: hidden; padding: 0; position: absolute; white-space: nowrap; width: 1px;`) on sibling `` if present. - **Rule:** If a visible text label exists in full mode, add `aria-hidden="true"` to the dot to prevent double announcement ("Active Active"). In compact mode, remove `aria-hidden` so `role="img"` provides the name. 3. **Status Text Mapping:** - `green` → `"Active"` (or product-specific term like `"Online"`) - `yellow` → `"Warning"` (or `"Pending"`) - `red` → `"Error"` (or `"Failing"`) - *Note:* Text must match product terminology exactly. Do not use `"green dot"` or `"status indicator"`. ## Phase 8 — Testing Strategy | Test Type | Scenario | Pass Criteria | |-----------|----------|---------------| | Automated | axe-core `color-contrast` & `aria-label` rules | No violations on ``. `role="img"` and `aria-label` present. | | Screen Reader | NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver focus/scan dot | Announces status text (e.g., "Active, image"), not shape/color. | | High Contrast | Windows HCM enabled + screen reader | Status meaning preserved via `aria-label`. Dot may lose color but remains announced. | | Compact Mode | Visually hidden label mode + screen reader | Label is visually gone but `aria-label` still announces status correctly. No double announcement. | | Contrast Audit | Dot against actual dashboard backgrounds (not white) | ≥3:1 contrast per WCAG 1.4.11 for all valid background combinations. | **Dynamic Prioritization:** Low risk component → prioritize screen reader verification and high-contrast mode testing over complex keyboard scenarios. ## Phase 9 — Implementation Tasks & Review Checkpoints ### Task 1: Update `` Component 🔍 **Review checkpoint after this task** **Files:** - `components/StatusDot.tsx` (or `.jsx`) - `components/StatusDot.css` **Structure Stub:** ```jsx ``` **ARIA Attributes:** - `role="img"`: Communicates semantic status per WCAG 1.1.1 - `aria-label`: Provides accessible name per WCAG 4.1.2 **Tests:** - Verify `aria-label` matches product terminology exactly - Verify no `title` attribute is used - Verify component does not accept `tabIndex` or become focusable **WCAG Criteria:** - WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content - WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value ### Task 2: Add Compact Mode CSS & Usage Guidelines 🔍 **Review checkpoint after this task** **Files:** - `styles/utilities.css` (add `.sr-only` class if missing) - Dashboard usage files (tables, sidebars, cards) **CSS Stub:** ```css .sr-only { clip: rect(0 0 0 0); clip-path: inset(50%); height: 1px; margin: -1px; overflow: hidden; padding: 0; position: absolute; white-space: nowrap; width: 1px; } ``` **Usage Logic:** - Full mode: `{statusText}` + dot with `aria-hidden="true"` - Compact mode: Only dot with `role="img" aria-label` (no `aria-hidden`) **Tests:** - Verify label is visually hidden but present in DOM/AT tree - Verify no double announcement in full mode - Verify compact mode announces correctly **WCAG Criteria:** - WCAG 1.3.2 Meaningful Sequence - WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value ### Task 3: Contrast & High Contrast Mode Validation 🔍 **Review checkpoint after this task** **Files:** - Design system token file (update hex values if needed) - Manual test script **Actions:** - Audit all dot/background combinations for ≥3:1 contrast (WCAG 1.4.11) - Test with Windows HCM enabled - Verify screen reader behavior in HCM **Tests:** - Contrast ratio meets 3:1 minimum against adjacent backgrounds - Status meaning preserved in high contrast mode via `aria-label` **WCAG Criteria:** - WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast - WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color --- ## a11y-Critic Review Checkpoints | Checkpoint | After Task | Focus Areas | |-----------|-----------|------------| | 🔍 1 | Task 1 | Verify `role="img"` + `aria-label` present. No `title`. No focusability. Correct status text mapping. | | 🔍 2 | Task 2 | Verify compact mode CSS hides visually but not in AT tree. Verify `aria-hidden` logic prevents double announcement. | | 🔍 3 | Task 3 | Verify ≥3:1 contrast against actual backgrounds (not white). Verify Windows HCM + screen reader behavior. | --- ## References - [WCAG 2.2 1.1.1 Non-text Content](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-content.html) - [WCAG 2.2 1.4.1 Use of Color](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/use-of-color.html) - [WCAG 2.2 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html) - [WCAG 2.2 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value.html) - [WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/) - [a11y-critic skill](https://github.com/zivtech/accessibility-skills) — for post-implementation review - [accessibility-testing skill](https://github.com/zivtech/zivtech-claude-skills) — for automated contrast & ARIA validation
